entities.summary: Manius Pomponius Matho was a Roman general and statesman who played a significant role in the late Roman Republic. Born in the 3rd century BCE, Matho rose to prominence during the Punic Wars, serving under the famous general Scipio Africanus. In 210 BCE, Matho was elected consul, a position he shared with Quintus Fabius Maximus Verrucosus. As consul, Matho oversaw the Roman campaign in Spain, where he distinguished himself in battle. Despite his military successes, Matho's legacy was largely eclipsed by that of his grandson, Scipio Africanus, who went on to become one of Rome's greatest generals. Nevertheless, Matho's contributions to Roman military strategy and politics remain an important chapter in the history of the Roman Republic. The Roman Senate's records from this period, as recorded by the ancient historian Polybius, provide valuable insight into Matho's career and the machinations of the Roman elite.
